en.title: Disjoint Subarrays Max Sum
en.description:
You must cut the array at some adjacent position into a non-empty left part and a non-empty right part, both contiguous. Find the maximum non-empty contiguous subarray sum of the left part and of the right part separately, then add the two; return the maximum over all cuts. The cut point and the maximum subarrays within the two parts may vary independently.

The input format, examples and test data were prepared by CSWork; see the statement for the original source and the limits added by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains n integers a[i]. The original statement gives no bounds on n or the values; this site adds 2≤n≤200000 and −1000000000≤a[i]≤1000000000, so that both parts are non-empty and the sums are safe in 64 bits.
en.output: Output one integer, the best sum over all valid cuts.
en.explanation: Process the input according to the rules above; see the companion notes for the approach, the correctness proof and the complexity.
hints: Precompute the maximum subarray sum within every prefix, and likewise within every suffix. Enumerate the cut point i and maximize prefixBest[i]+suffixBest[i+1].
